title: Boreal Threshold — Climate-Tech Mission Hero
description: A full-bleed earth-tone landscape photograph anchors a ranged-left display-sans problem statement, a top-right monospace wordmark, and a single high-contrast impact-metric chip — blending documentary-photography gravity with stripped startup clarity.
philosophy: This template exists for the moment when data alone cannot convey urgency and the room needs to feel the stakes before it hears the numbers. It deliberately rejects the glossy blue-gradient aesthetic of legacy enterprise decks in favour of something closer to photojournalism: raw terrain, unadorned type, and a solitary yellow chip that earns its colour precisely because it is the only warm note on screen. It is built for founders who understand that conviction and decoration are enemies. The monospace wordmark signals craft-without-vanity, reinforcing a recycled-material ethos rather than a Silicon Valley sheen.
goodFor: 3-line emissions or climate-impact problem statements on the opening hero slide
Series A and B cleantech or climate-fund investor pitches
Conference keynote openers where large screen size amplifies landscape photography
Mission-first 'why we exist' moments in impact-investing decks
avoidFor: Chart-heavy quarterly financial reviews requiring data density
Consumer lifestyle or CPG product showcases needing bright, celebratory moods
Multi-column bento or dashboard layouts with more than two content zones
Brands whose visual identity depends on a clean white or pastel-dominant canvas
author: harness

examples.promptCore: The slide opens like a documentary frame — vast, consequential terrain, deliberately raw and unadorned. A boreal landscape bleeds edge-to-edge, lending gravity no data point can rival; the sparse left-ranged title anchors the lower canvas with carved authority. The sole warm impact chip earns its chromatic intensity precisely because every other element dissolves into earth and shadow. Avoid gradient overlays, decorative motifs, or any embellishment that softens the photojournalistic severity.
examples.layoutNotes: Full-bleed landscape photograph spans edge-to-edge with zero border break, set as a base layer behind all type. A 12-column grid with an 8% outer gutter governs placement: wordmark locks top-right in cols 9–12 flush to the upper margin; primary title spans cols 1–7 in the lower third, baseline sitting approximately 30% from the bottom edge. The impact-metric chip is left-aligned immediately beneath the title block, acting as a typographic full stop. No header band or footer rule; hierarchy is carried by scale contrast and the chip's singular chromatic accent.

examples.promptCore: The slide reads like a captioned field photograph from a climate investigation — still, pressured, and deliberately uncomfortable in its silence. Compositional weight is split between a raw left-anchored statement that unfolds slowly and a lone mustard chip on the right that detonates a single number into the void between them. The asymmetry is load-bearing: resist the urge to balance with icons, secondary columns, or illustrative diagrams. The mood should feel like evidence laid on a table, not a dashboard designed to reassure.

examples.layoutNotes: 12-column grid, full-bleed photograph behind all content with a deepened terrain overlay concentrated toward the lower half. Primary content zone — a two-to-three-line impact statement plus a terse supporting clause — occupies cols 1–7, anchored to the lower-third horizontal and flush to an 8% left margin. A single metric chip (large numeral + unit + descriptor line) floats isolated in cols 9–11, vertically aligned to the impact statement's cap-height, separated from it by deliberate negative space rather than a rule. Monospace section tag persists top-right as on the hero; a minimal source attribution in small monospace sits directly beneath the chip; page number bottom-right outside the primary zone.
